summary: An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Robert Alexander Neil studied at the University of Aberdeen and Cambridge under Geddes, Cowell, Verrall, Reid, and Shilleto. He was a Fellow and Senior Tutor at Pembroke College and Cambridge University Lecturer in Sanskrit.
Robert Anderson worked in Indology and linguistics. He was educated at Harrow School and the East India Company College, where he later served as Assistant Professor from 1821 to 1825.

A scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology, Robert Anthony Orsi studied at Trinity College, Hartford, and Yale. He held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard, and Northwestern, and was a Faculty Fellow at Notre Dame (2020–2021).

Working in Indology and religious studies, Robert Antoine earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He taught Sanskrit at St. Xavier's Collegiate School in 1951 and was Reader in literature at Jadavpur University beginning in 1956.

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Robert Arrowsmith studied at Columbia and Berlin. He taught at Columbia, Racine College, and Teachers College, served as principal of two schools, and worked as an editor for the American Book Company (1894–1913).

Robert Atkinson worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Trinity College Dublin and the University of Liège. He held professorships at Trinity College Dublin and Trinity College, Hartford, and served as president of the Royal Irish Academy (1901–1906).

Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Hawaiʻi and UC Berkeley, studying under D. T. Suzuki and R. H. Blyth. He held posts at the East-West Center and University of Hawaiʻi.

Robert Barkley Shaw was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He was educated at Marlborough College from circa 1853 to 1856 and at Trinity College, Cambridge, from circa 1856 to 1858.

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist educated at the University of Cambridge. He served as Adjunct Professor at Columbia University (~1999–2018), directed a summer program at Tibet University (2000–2006), and became a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS around 2018.

Tibetologist, Central Asianist, and linguist Robert Bleichsteiner earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bittner, Schroeder, and Geiger. He became a professor at the University of Vienna and was appointed Director of the Weltmuseum Wien in 1945.

Robert Boxberger worked in Indology and linguistics, having studied at the University of Jena under August Schleicher. He served as a teacher at Realschule Erfurt (1858–1876) and as a librarian at the Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek (1868–1876).

A Tibetologist and religious studies scholar, Robert Brainerd Ekvall studied at Wheaton College, Nyack College, and the University of Chicago. He held research positions at the University of Chicago, the University of Washington, and the Burke Museum.

Robert Bruce Foote was an archaeologist and geologist. He worked as Superintendent at the Geological Survey of India (1858–1891), was employed by Baroda State in 1892, and became Director of the Mysore Geological Department in 1894.

Robert Caesar Childers specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama Thera, later serving as Sub-Librarian at the India Office and Professor of Pali at University College London.

Robert Chalmers specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Oriel College, Oxford, under Edwin Abbott Abbott and T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society and was Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indology and legal scholar educated at Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford, Principal of New Inn Hall, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, and President of The Asiatic Society.

Robert Charles Zaehner studied at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. Specializing in religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies, he was Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics at Oxford and a Fellow of All Souls College (1952–1974).

Robert Cotton Mather was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at the University of Edinburgh, earned an M.A. from the University of Glasgow by 1831, and attended Homerton College from circa 1831 to 1833.

Robert DeCaroli is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount, joining George Mason University around 2002.

Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1981 to 1985. He held positions at the University of Kerala and became a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain around 1989.
